title: Terragrunt and our infrastructure repo
bridge: Terragrunt is like npm workspaces for Terraform. It has one shared root config, one folder per piece, and a command that runs them all in order. Except Terragrunt only writes files and calls tofu. The resources, plans and state are still OpenTofu's.
intro: The infrastructure repo holds hundreds of small OpenTofu runs, one per folder. Terragrunt glues them together: it writes the backend settings, passes shared tags, and runs folders in dependency order. This lesson maps the repo and builds a small copy of the ai-agents tree on your laptop.

picture.caption: A unit includes the root, reads its account's facts, points at a module, and gets its own state; dependencies set the order.

steps.text: include: pulls in the backend, providers and common inputs
reads the account name, the role to assume and the tags
terraform.source names the module to run
copies the module, writes backend.tf, runs tofu; state key = the unit's path
dependency "vpc": reads the VPC unit's outputs, so it runs after it

p: The infrastructure repo has an old tree and a new one. The old tree starts at root.hcl in the repo root and lives under multi_tenant/accounts/<account>/<component>/. The inf cluster's tools, such as n8n and Vault, live there, in multi_tenant/accounts/infrastructure/.

The new tree starts at terraform/root.hcl and lives under terraform/accounts/<account>/<cloud>/<region or global>/<component>/. New accounts go here. G3-02 adds terraform/accounts/ai-agents/, copied from the solutions account.
sections.because: We learn the layout first because every infra ticket starts with 'which folder does this go in?'.

code.text:
terraform/
├── root.hcl                          backend, providers, common inputs
├── common.hcl                        provider versions (aws 6.64.0, helm 3.1.1, ...)
└── accounts/ai-agents/
    ├── account.hcl                   account name, role to assume, tags
    └── aws/
        ├── cloud.hcl
        ├── global/
        │   ├── region.hcl
        │   └── iam/github-actions/terragrunt.hcl     the CI role (p3-1)
        └── us-east-1/
            ├── region.hcl
            ├── core-services/vpc/terragrunt.hcl      the sandbox VPC (G3-04)
            ├── core-services/runs-bucket/terragrunt.hcl
            ├── core-services/dns-firewall/terragrunt.hcl
            └── sandboxes/terragrunt.hcl              launch templates and pools (G3-11)

notes.text: Every unit below includes this file.
One per account. Units find it by walking up the folders.
global/ is for things with no region, such as IAM.
One folder per component. Each is a unit with its own state.

sections.h: A unit is one folder and one state
p: A unit is a folder with a terragrunt.hcl. It names one module and its inputs, and gets its own state. Running plan in a unit plans only that unit.

Here is G3-04's VPC unit. Notice the // in the source. Terragrunt copies everything before // into its cache, so the module can still reach its neighbours with ../. Everything after // is the folder to run.
sections.because: We keep one component per unit because a small state means a small plan, and a mistake touches one thing.

notes.text: Walks up the folders until it finds root.hcl, and merges it in.
expose = true lets this file read the root's locals, as include.root.locals.
The folder of root.hcl, up one level, then modules/. The // marks where the copy stops.
Reads account.hcl as data, so its locals can be used here.
Inputs become the module's variables, like props.
The account's tags, so every resource is labelled the same way.

sections.h: The root: backend and shared inputs
p: root.hcl is included by every unit. Its remote_state block says where state lives. In our repo that is the S3 bucket rhinohealth-terraform-state, with the key ${path_relative_to_include()}/terraform.tfstate and use_lockfile = true. Each unit's state key is its path, so no two units share a state.

Terragrunt writes the backend block into a generated backend.tf before it runs tofu. The root also passes common inputs and generates provider blocks that assume the account's TerraformDeploymentRole. Below is the lab copy, with a local file instead of S3.
sections.because: We use a local backend in the lab because the real bucket needs company credentials, and the shape is the same.

notes.text: Evaluated for each unit, so it finds that unit's own account.hcl.
Real repo: backend = "s3" with bucket, key, region and use_lockfile = true.
path_relative_to_include() is the unit's path below this file, so every unit gets its own state.
Writes backend.tf into the unit's working copy, replacing any older one.
Every unit gets tags without repeating them.

p: account.hcl holds what is true for every unit in one account. That is its name, the role Terragrunt assumes, a name prefix and the tags. Vanta, our compliance tool, reads the Vanta tags.
G3-02 writes this file for ai-agents. The name prefix is ai-agents, never agents: in this repo 'rhino-agent' already means a Rhino Client VM.
sections.because: We put account facts in one file because tags and role ARNs copied into units drift apart.

code.text:
locals {
  account_name = "ai-agents"
  project      = "rhinofcp"

  # Created in Control Tower; TerraformDeploymentRole was bootstrapped by hand (see README).
  assume_role_arn = "arn:aws:iam::<AI_AGENTS_ACCOUNT_ID>:role/TerraformDeploymentRole"

  # Prefix for sandbox resources. Not "agents": in this repo that word means Rhino Client VMs.
  name_prefix = "ai-agents"

  tags = {
    account_name          = "ai-agents"
    VantaNonProd          = "true"
    VantaContainsUserData = "false" # fake seed data only, never PHI
    VantaOwner            = "tal@example.com"
    created_by            = "terraform"
    project               = "rhinofcp"
  }
}

notes.text: New accounts use project rhinofcp.
The role every plan and apply in this account assumes. G7-30 makes the role name switchable for read-only plans.
Used in resource names: ai-agents-sandbox-lite and so on.
A promise to Vanta: no user data here. Keeping PHI out of sandboxes makes it true.

p: A dependency block lets one unit read another unit's outputs. The sandboxes unit needs the VPC's subnet IDs, so it depends on the vpc unit. That also sets the order: vpc runs first.
On the very first plan, the vpc unit has no state yet, so it has no outputs. mock_outputs gives placeholder values for plan and validate only. Apply never uses them.
sections.because: We allow mocks only for plan and validate because a mock subnet ID must never reach a real apply.

notes.text: A relative path to the unit we read from.
Placeholder outputs. The fake value 10.0.0.0/18 makes it obvious in a plan.
Mocks are refused for apply, so a real apply always reads real outputs.
The dependency's outputs, used like any value.

p: terragrunt run --all -- plan runs plan in every unit below the current folder, in dependency order. Older docs call it run-all. terragrunt list --dag prints the units in that order without running anything.

In our repo, CI only checks formatting today. The author runs plan locally over VPN, pastes it into the PR, and a DevOps reviewer applies (G3-02, G3-04). G7-32 will post read-only plans on PRs. Nobody runs run --all apply from an agent, ever.
sections.because: We list the order before we plan because a wrong dependency shows up here, before any tofu run.

code.text:
terragrunt list --dag
terragrunt run --all --non-interactive -- plan
(cd core-services/vpc && terragrunt apply -auto-approve)   # lab only
(cd sandboxes && terragrunt plan 2>&1 | grep -o '10\.60\.[0-9]*\.0/18' | sort -u)

notes.text: Units in run order: vpc first, because sandboxes depends on it.
Everything after -- goes to tofu. --non-interactive answers prompts for you.
Gives vpc real state and outputs. In the repo, a person applies.
The plan now shows the real subnets instead of the mock.

sections.h: The n8n pattern for services on inf
p: Services that run on the inf cluster are not in the new tree. They are units in the old tree, under multi_tenant/accounts/infrastructure/<tool>/, one unit per piece. n8n is the model: iam, secrets, rds, sg, elasticache, s3 and repository units, plus an n8n.hcl with the shared facts.

The agents' Temporal (G3-06) and services (G3-17) copy that shape under multi_tenant/accounts/infrastructure/ai-agents/. The repository unit installs a Helm chart with a helm_release; p5-2 walks through it.

callout.text: Module references differ by tree. New tree: "${get_parent_terragrunt_dir("root")}/..//modules/<m>/". Old tree: "../../../../modules/<m>//". Registry: "tfr:///terraform-aws-modules/<m>/aws//.?version=x". The repo uses no git:: sources.

lab.faded: Add a third unit, core-services/runs-bucket. Its module fake-bucket has a terraform_data with input = { name = var.name } and an output name. Its input is name = "rhino-ai-agents-runs". Left to you: make sandboxes depend on it too, with a second dependency block and its own mock_outputs. Check with terragrunt list --dag that sandboxes now runs last.
lab.alone: Copy terraform/accounts/ai-agents to terraform/accounts/solutions-lab with its own account.hcl (account_name solutions-lab). From terraform/accounts, run terragrunt run --all --non-interactive -- plan. Their units have the same names. Use the state paths to explain why the two accounts still never share a state file.
lab.done: list --dag shows vpc before sandboxes, and the first plan uses the mock subnet. After you apply vpc, the sandboxes plan shows the three real /18s.

quiz.q: Where does a unit's state live in our repo?

options.text: In S3, bucket rhinohealth-terraform-state, at the unit's path below root.hcl plus /terraform.tfstate
options.why: path_relative_to_include() makes the key, so every unit has its own state.

options.text: In the unit's folder, committed to git
options.why: State can hold secrets and must be locked; it never goes in git.

options.text: In one state file per account
options.why: One per unit. A small state means a small plan.

options.text: Faking a unit's outputs in production when it is broken
options.why: Mocks are refused for apply by mock_outputs_allowed_terraform_commands.
They exist so plan can run in order, not for tests.

options.text: Letting plan and validate run before the unit they depend on has state
options.why: On the first plan of a new account, nothing has outputs yet.

quiz.q: Where does the new ai-agents AWS account's code go?

options.text: multi_tenant/accounts/ai-agents/, next to the inf tools
options.why: That is the old tree. New accounts go in the new one.
G3-02 copies the solutions account and drops the GCP parts.

options.text: A new repository only for agents
options.why: All AWS accounts live in the infrastructure repo, owned by DevOps.

words.plain: A tool that writes backend and provider files and runs tofu in many folders, in order.
One folder with a terragrunt.hcl: one module, its inputs, and its own state.
The file every unit includes, with the backend, providers and common inputs.
A block that merges a parent file, usually root.hcl, into a unit.
A block that reads another unit's outputs and makes it run first.
Placeholder outputs for plan and validate while the other unit has no state yet.
Run one tofu command in every unit below a folder, in dependency order (formerly run-all).

tickets.why: Adds terraform/accounts/ai-agents/ with account.hcl and the region files, copied from solutions.
The core-services units: vpc, runs-bucket, dns-firewall and private-zone, planned locally and applied by a person.
Temporal on inf copies the n8n pattern: one folder of units in the old tree.
The agent services are more units in that folder, plus a PrivateLink unit.

remember: One folder is one unit and one state. root.hcl writes the plumbing, account.hcl holds the facts, and dependencies set the order.
